title: In 1973, a Town Beat a Volcano With 6 Billion Litres of Seawater

scenes.text: In 1973, a town fought a volcano with seawater. And won.
Heimaey, Iceland. At two in the morning a crack opened beside the town and poured lava.
All 5,300 people fled on fishing boats within hours.
Then the lava turned toward the harbour. Block it, and the town is dead.
So they pumped the sea onto it. Fifty pumps, 1,000 litres a second, for five months. Six billion litres.
The lava froze 100 metres from the harbour mouth. They beat a volcano with a hose.

description:
On 23 January 1973 the Eldfell eruption began on the Icelandic island of Heimaey, and all 5,300 residents were evacuated by the fishing fleet within hours.
When the lava threatened to seal the harbour, crews pumped about 6 million cubic metres of seawater onto the flow from February to July, using around 50 pumps flown in from the United States. The lava stopped about 100 metres short of the harbour entrance.
Would you have gone back to live next to the new volcano? Comment below.
first_comment: The water turned about 4 million cubic metres of lava to rock, and the island grew by 2.5 square kilometres. Roughly 400 homes were buried. Would you have stayed to man the pumps?
